objective: Use a full-scale manual separating screen to recover dry ceramic finishing media into a receiver while retaining every representative steel washer, then return the released screen stably to both supports. This frozen rigid-PhysX specification defines future construction and qualification; it does not claim native qualification or robot success.
instruction: Pour the dry mixture into the separating screen. Manipulate the screen to recover the ceramic media in the receiver while retaining every metal washer. Return the screen to both supports and release it.
industrial_mapping: Provisional category: Impact on jobs. Raytech mass-finishing documentation establishes manual screening as a dry parts/media separation operation. The tested ability combines controlled pouring, bimanual load sharing, orientation-dependent aperture passage, bridge release, spill prevention, workpiece retention, supported replacement, and collision-free release. Generic pouring, visual sorting, and homogeneous-object transfer are real alternatives but do not test selective physical screening. Novelty and occupational-scale importance remain subject to independent review.
damage_rules: Freeze at reset media assemblies M={m01…m24}, washer assemblies A={a01…a04}, washer segments WS={a01s01…a04s04}, and convex collider sets SC, RC, SU, FC, GR, ENV for screen, receiver, supports, feed cup, robot/grippers, and table/floor. Count an intact washer assembly once in admitted mass.

For completed production interval k: resolve physics; read native poses, velocities, joint-break events, derived joint-frame states, full-geometry signed distances, contacts, and impulses; convert pair-summed impulse J to step-average force |J|/(1/240 s); advance causal transfer and passage state; latch immutable events and damage; recompute containment, recovery, support, clearance, and dwell; then compute score. Process O_57600 before timeout. Reports at 20 Hz use the latest completed physics sample.

Derive each washer-joint and screen-hinge relative transform from both native body poses and authored local joint frames. Joint angle is signed relative rotation about the authored hinge axis. Log translation and off-axis residuals independently; root roll, constants, and invented joint sensors are invalid substitutes.

Let delta=0.0005 m. For each moving convex collider section intersecting the screen-floor slab, aperture_margin is signed distance to that aperture's fixed polygon AP, positive inside. rib_clearance is swept signed distance to every physical rib, positive when disjoint. A valid passage interval requires both minima >=-delta and verified conservative advancement with rotational subdivision bounded so unobserved surface travel is <=delta/2. Endpoint-only samples cannot establish passage.

Receiver containment requires every transformed convex part and every conservatively swept edge to remain inside closed receiver volume RV, allowing supported floor or side-wall overlap no deeper than delta. Over-rim exit, bottom escape, wall penetration deeper than delta, invalid entry, later exit, off-path loss, contamination, or inaccessibility permanently revokes eligibility; re-entry cannot clear a latched event.

Each intact assembly follows FEED→EXITED_FEED→FREE_FLIGHT→ENTERED_SCREEN. EXITED_FEED is an outward swept crossing through the cup mouth. FREE_FLIGHT requires two consecutive completed physics samples disjoint from cup and screen. ENTERED_SCREEN is a later inward swept crossing through the screen rim. Every segment of an intact washer must transition consistently.

A medium gains persistent causal_passage only after valid admission and genuine whole-collider aperture passage. Recovery eligibility is recomputed every physics sample and revoked by loss of full receiver containment or any immutable prerequisite.

Invalid provenance from direct robot contact is evaluated only on collider pairs GR–M and GR–WS. At each completed 240 Hz post-solve sample, contact_pair(g,b)=1 iff a required robot/gripper collider g and an individual medium or washer-segment collider b have a native contact point with positive normal impulse or full-geometry signed distance <=0. For each pair, a segment starts on the first true sample, accumulates consecutive completed intervals, resets to zero on the first false sample, and is discarded at reset or episode end if shorter than 12 intervals. Reaching 12 consecutive intervals (0.05 s) latches invalid provenance before scoring that sample; shorter incidental contact is exempt from direct-contact provenance only and cannot clear another staging, spill, damage, or contamination event. Separate staging latches when an individual medium or washer segment is externally supported by GR, SU, or ENV while outside both FC and SC for 12 consecutive intervals, using the same start/reset/end convention. Receiver entry before genuine screening, non-mouth cup departure, inconsistent segment admission, or unauthorized pre-admission separation remains an immediate immutable zero-score fault.

Define screen retained volume SV from the authored inner rim surfaces and the physical floor/rib top support surface; its signed side margin is positive inward and its signed support clearance is positive above the top surface. A retained M or WS collider is full_inside_screen iff every transformed convex part and every conservatively swept edge has side margin >=-delta and support clearance >=-delta, and no part has crossed the floor-bottom surface, a non-aperture floor region, or a rib by more than delta. Supported floor/rib/rim overlap up to delta is numerical contact tolerance, not passage. During a registered genuine aperture passage only, the AP and swept-rib rules govern crossing; after EXIT the body is no longer required to be in SV. Over-rim exit, floor-bottom crossing without genuine passage, or wall/rib penetration deeper than delta latches media spill or washer loss as applicable.

Receiver contamination is closed over frozen contaminant collider set C=SC union SU union FC union GR union ENV union WS, explicitly excluding RC itself and all media M. It latches when any convex part or conservatively swept edge of c in C has positive-volume intersection with RV eroded inward by delta, equivalently interior penetration deeper than delta. Boundary touch and supported RC floor/side-wall overlap no deeper than delta do not count. Media spill separately latches on over-rim exit, off-path ENV contact, invalid receiver entry, receiver exit, penetration deeper than delta, or inaccessibility; washer loss separately latches on over-rim exit, ENV contact outside RC, inaccessibility, or floor-bottom crossing without genuine passage.

Each washer has four breakable fixed joints with assumed 200 N break-force limits. fracture(a) latches only on a native PhysX joint-break event or relative-frame error exceeding 0.0005 m translation or 0.5 deg rotation. Force threshold alone is diagnostic and cannot establish fracture.

permanent_deformation(a) is the rigid proxy where, after external washer contact ends and every segment remains below 0.01 m/s linear and 0.05 rad/s angular speed for 0.5 s, an intact joint's relative-frame translation error exceeds 0.00025 m or rotation error exceeds 0.25 deg throughout that settling window. This assumed proxy is not real plasticity. Retained fracture or deformation caps score at 0.40; fragment loss is a zero-score hard failure.

Define workspace WV={-0.55<=x<=0.55,-0.05<=y<=0.75,-0.02<=z<=0.75} m. A collider is inaccessible if any vertex leaves WV, any collider falls below z=-0.02 m, or the complete collider is physically trapped while all four frozen approach prisms are obstructed. IK failure alone is not inaccessibility.

Any post-reset pose or velocity write to M, WS, SC, RC, SU, or FC; fake grasp weld; required-collider disablement; particle freezing; hidden restoring force; teleport; or unlogged physics substitution is a permanent zero-score fault. Spill, loss, fracture, deformation, excessive contact, and escape remain physically possible.

Reset all accumulators, causal records, event segments, fault latches, damage flags, eligibility flags, and dwell clocks between trials. An event segment begins on the first true post-solve sample and ends on the first subsequent false sample; durations equal completed intervals times dt. Physics and collision checks use post-solve physics samples; camera checks use rendered 20 Hz frames. Control samples cannot prove substep behavior.
assets: Full-scale separating screen: sourced outer diameter 0.3683 m and depth 0.0635 m; assumed 0.003 m walls/floor, 0.150 m perforated radius, 0.0127 m square apertures, 0.003 m ribs, 0.0157 m pitch, 0.40 kg mass, and two grasp tabs.

Twenty-four free rigid ceramic angle-cut media bodies: sourced diameter 0.009525 m and axial envelope 0.022225 m; assumed 15 deg cuts and 2500 kg/m^3 density; frozen mesh mass 0.0034820220468 kg each.

Four representative steel washer assemblies: 0.030 m outer diameter, 0.008 m bore, 0.004 m thickness, density 7850 kg/m^3, four rigid arc segments, four breakable fixed joints, and analytic assembly mass 0.0206170159 kg.
Rigid receiver 0.45 by 0.40 by 0.08 m with 0.005 m floor/walls; two 0.52 by 0.015 by 0.010 m support beams; feed cup outer diameter 0.078 m, height 0.100 m, and 0.003 m walls/floor.
Pinned public YAM asset and guarded 14D joint-action interface; production dt=1/240 s, 20 Hz controls held for 12 completed physics intervals, and paired refinement dt=1/480 s.
Industrial evidence: preserved Raytech manual-screening, ceramic-media, and separation guidance. Third-party assets require license disclosure; task-specific geometry is independently authored.
approximations: Only dry rigid-body separation is modeled; polishing, abrasion, liquid, wet cohesion, dust, wear, lubrication, and true plastic deformation are excluded.

Aperture geometry, screen mass, tabs, media cuts/density, fixtures, representative washers, four-segment damage proxy, 200 N threshold, and diagnostic fixtures are disclosed engineering assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD or calibrated commercial limits.

Uncalibrated contacts are ceramic/polymer static/dynamic friction 0.50/0.35, steel/polymer 0.45/0.35, media/media 0.40/0.30, restitution 0.05, contact offset 0.00015 m, rest offset 0 m, and 32/8 solver position/velocity iterations. The 180 N force limit, penetration limits, stability limits, joint margins, and dwell thresholds are explicit assumptions requiring native qualification.

delta=0.0005 m applies to dynamic penetration, aperture-section margin, swept-rib distance, retained screen floor/rib/rim supported contact, and supported receiver contact. It is numerical tolerance only: authored collision geometry and AP remain unchanged; it permits neither center-only containment, passage through a rib or non-aperture floor, floor-bottom escape, nor positive-volume receiver contamination deeper than delta.

Index aperture polygons by integer grid coordinate (u,v), lexicographically by v then u, retaining only complete 0.0127 m squares whose closure lies within the 0.150 m perforated-radius circle. AP(0,0), centered at the screen-frame origin with edges parallel to +Xscreen and +Yscreen, is the unique central aperture used by all diagnostic protocols. Screen-frame +Z points upward. World orientations use active extrinsic Rz(yaw)Ry(pitch)Rx(roll), applied right-to-left.

End-first trials use yaw degrees [0,18,36,54,72,90,108,126,144,162,180,198,216,234,252,270,288,306,324,342], roll=0, pitch=0. Place the medium center at AP(0,0) center plus 0.010 m +Zscreen, long axis within 5 deg of -gravity, with the lowest collider point initially >=0.001 m above every screen collider; zero velocity; simulate 1.0 s. Success is genuine whole-collider passage without immutable event.

Transverse trials use the same ordered yaw list with roll=0 and pitch=90 deg, identical carrier transform, clearance, reset, and 1.0 s gravity-only interval. Report genuine passages/20; no rejected or replacement trial is allowed.

Bridge trials start from the 20 transverse transforms. A trial qualifies only if supported by at least two distinct ribs for 0.5 s. At qualification time tq set screen hinge angle theta(t)=5 deg*sin(2*pi*(t-tq) Hz) for tq<=t<=tq+2 s, starting at zero angle with positive angular velocity; thereafter theta=0. Use native hinge drive only, seed=788900+i, and simulate through tq+2.5 s. Success is genuine passage. Exactly 20 qualifying trials must be obtained from seeds 788901 upward; log every rejected seed without replacement concealment.

Washer escape uses carrier screen transform position (0,0,0.20) m world and identity orientation, with supports at x-axis beams y=+/-0.17 m and top z=0.20 m. For each a01…a04 use (roll,pitch,yaw) degrees [(0,0,0),(0,0,45),(0,0,90),(90,0,0),(90,0,45),(90,0,90),(0,45,0),(0,45,90),(45,45,0),(45,45,90)]. Center assembly over AP(0,0); choose center height so its lowest collider point is exactly 0.010 m above the floor top and initially disjoint by >=0.001 m; zero velocity; simulate 2.0 s. Any segment crossing below the floor-bottom plane is escape. Reset all state after each of 40 trials.

Bore lodging uses a washer carrier with center (0,0,0.20) m, identity orientation, bore prism equal to the exact 0.008 m-diameter washer hole extruded from z=-0.002 to +0.002 m in washer coordinates, and a fixed annular support outside radius 0.015 m that never intersects the bore prism. The washer itself is unconstrained after release. Media orientations are yaw [0,36,72,108,144] crossed with pitch [0,45,90,135] deg, roll=0, ordered pitch-major. Put the media center 0.005 m above the washer top with initial clearance >=0.001 m, zero velocities, and simulate 2.0 s. Lodging requires full-collider intersection with the bore prism for 0.5 consecutive seconds while neither body has external constraint or robot contact.

The external-force diagnostic uses a frozen bilateral trajectory: screen starts supported at pose p0=(0,0.25,0.22) m and identity orientation; grippers close symmetrically on tab centers for 0.50 s, then the commanded screen reference rises linearly by 0.030 m during 0.50 s and remains fixed for 3.00 s. Both tab-relative gripper transforms remain constant; joint actions are guarded and held at 20 Hz. Aggregate SC contacts against GR, SU, ENV as max_k |sum J_pair,k|/dt. Qualification requires <=180 N and no damage or hard failure.

The required signed-distance manifest is SC–SU; SC–FC; SC–RC; SC–ENV; SC–GR; M–SC; M–FC; M–RC; M–SU; M–ENV; M–GR; M–M for distinct media; M–WS; WS–SC; WS–FC; WS–RC; WS–SU; WS–ENV; WS–GR; and WS–WS between different washer assemblies or non-adjacent segments of one assembly. Exclude only same rigid body, authored adjacent washer segments joined together, robot self-collision pairs filtered by the pinned YAM asset, and valid RC-supported floor/wall contacts up to delta. Missing, unsupported, or unexpectedly filtered manifest pairs fail qualification. Aggregate SC–SU separately at 0.001 m; every other included dynamic pair uses 0.0005 m.

The paired-refinement manifest uses reset seed 7889, the exact frozen initial transforms from the production scene, and the same 4,800 timestamped 14D actions indexed n=0…4799 at t=n/20 s, held piecewise constant. Independent resets clear all records. The 240 Hz replay takes 12 intervals per action and the 480 Hz replay takes 24. Both process the fixed t=240 s terminal sample even if Q becomes true earlier; only immutable hard failure may terminate, in which case final r is sampled immediately after the failure sample and the same remaining actions are not executed. Compare terminal r and immutable event-type sets.

Existing aperture, mass/inertia, pose-API, joint-break, and hinge-drive probes are component evidence only. Full swept passage, retention, bridge release, bore lodging, complete environment physics, robot manipulation, scoring controls, paired refinement, and fresh demonstrations remain unverified.

Scripted experts may read poses, velocities, derived joint states, contacts, and scorer flags to plan guarded actions. Such reads do not alter model observations and never permit task-object state writes, teleports, welds, collision disabling, freezing, or hidden forces.

Camera validity is evaluated at rendered 20 Hz. RGB pixels must be finite and encoded; depth pixels finite and positive. Required visibility means screen, cup, receiver, one complete medium, and one complete washer are each visible in at least 80% of control frames.
scoring_spec: At reset freeze M, A, WS, masses, convex parts, AP, SV, receiver volume RV, workspace WV, contaminant set C, fixtures, and approach prisms. Let M0 be the sum of all 24 media and four washer-assembly masses and MM0 the media mass. valid_admission(b)=1 only after b completes FEED→EXITED_FEED→FREE_FLIGHT→ENTERED_SCREEN without invalid provenance. F=clamp(sum_b(m_b*valid_admission(b))/M0,0,1). causal_passage(i)=1 persistently only after valid admission and a genuine whole-collider aperture crossing satisfying continuous swept AP/rib rules. full_inside_screen(i,k)=1 iff every convex part and conservatively swept edge has SV inner-rim side margin >=-delta and floor/rib-top support clearance >=-delta, with no floor-bottom, non-aperture-floor, or rib crossing deeper than delta; only a registered genuine AP passage uses the separate swept crossing rule. eligible_receiver(i,k)=1 iff causal_passage(i)=1; every convex part and swept edge satisfies full RV containment with supported overlap no deeper than delta; and i has never spilled, exited RV, become inaccessible, penetrated an RC wall deeper than delta, entered by an invalid path, or incurred invalid provenance. The term receiver-contained everywhere in this contract means eligible_receiver(i,k)=1, not merely a current center or pose test. complete_loading holds iff all 28 assemblies are validly admitted, every washer segment or fragment is currently full_inside_screen, and every medium is either full_inside_screen or receiver-contained. Define r=clamp(sum_i(m_i*eligible_receiver(i,k))/MM0,0,1); eligibility is recomputed and revocable every physics sample. washer_retained requires every segment or fragment inside the screen and, for undamaged washers, all authored joints intact and no permanent_deformation. supported requires resolved contact on both support beams, screen height within 0.002 m of support top, |roll|<=3 deg, |pitch|<=3 deg, and screen-center projection within x=[-0.26,0.26], y=[0.15,0.35] m. clear requires signed distance from every gripper collider to SC union M union WS/fragments >=0.060 m. A hard failure is washer loss, media spill, receiver contamination, invalid provenance, forbidden mutation, or invalid continuous passage/tunneling. Q=1 iff complete_loading, F=1, r>=0.98, washer_retained, supported, clear, and no hard failure. Dwell begins at k0 when Q first becomes true; that sample contributes zero elapsed time. D=1 only while Q remains true through k-k0>=720 consecutive completed 240 Hz intervals. Any false prerequisite resets k0 and revokes D. Base B=0.20F+0.70*clamp(r/0.98,0,1)+0.10D. Final score is 0 after any hard failure; otherwise min(B,0.40) after retained fracture or permanent deformation, and B when undamaged. Report at 20 Hz from the latest completed physics sample and process O_57600 before timeout. Untouched score=0; complete loading with no recovery=0.20; 12 of 24 equal-mass eligible media=0.5571428571; threshold recovery without dwell=0.90; valid released three-second dwell=1.00. Hand identity, action count, shake count, and prescribed order are not graded.

required_controls.name: control_untouched_reset_zero
required_controls.reason: Fresh reset, no hard failure, all assemblies in FC, F=r=D=0.

required_controls.name: control_complete_loading_zero_recovery
required_controls.reason: All assemblies validly admitted inside SC; F=1,r=0,D=0, without damage or hard failure.

required_controls.name: control_half_recovery_baseline
required_controls.reason: F=1, exactly 12 equal-mass media eligible in RV, washers retained, D=0, without damage or hard failure.

required_controls.name: control_threshold_recovery_unreleased
required_controls.reason: F=1,r>=0.98, washers retained, but support or clearance false, so D=0.

required_controls.name: control_released_supported_full_dwell
required_controls.reason: F=1,r>=0.98, washers retained, supported and clear for 720 completed intervals.

required_controls.name: control_timeout_exact_720_dwell
required_controls.reason: Q is true from O_56880 through processed O_57600, exactly 720 completed intervals.

required_controls.name: control_timeout_719_dwell
required_controls.reason: Threshold-recovery baseline holds but Q spans only 719 completed intervals.

required_controls.name: control_early_passage_then_loading
required_controls.reason: Causal passages occur before final admission; later F=1,r>=0.98,D=0 without fault.

required_controls.name: control_receiver_exit_revokes_early_passage
required_controls.reason: A previously eligible medium exits RV; immutable spill overrides progress.

required_controls.name: control_retained_fracture_cap
required_controls.reason: An otherwise full-score state has a native joint break while all fragments remain in SC.

required_controls.name: control_retained_deformation_cap
required_controls.reason: An otherwise full-score state satisfies the settled deformation proxy without fragment loss.

required_controls.name: control_force_without_damage
required_controls.reason: Threshold recovery holds with D=0; diagnostic force reaches 200 N but no fracture or deformation predicate occurs.

required_controls.name: control_supported_receiver_contact_tolerance
required_controls.reason: Threshold recovery holds with D=0 and all media satisfy full eligible_receiver containment with supported overlap <=delta.

required_controls.name: control_receiver_wall_breach_failure
required_controls.reason: A medium penetrates an RC wall deeper than delta, latching spill.

required_controls.name: control_valid_full_collider_passage
required_controls.reason: F=1,r>=0.98,D=0 and every credited passage satisfies whole-collider AP and swept-rib margins >=-delta.

required_controls.name: control_rib_sweep_breach_failure
required_controls.reason: Swept rib overlap deeper than delta or an unqualified continuous crossing latches invalid passage.

required_controls.name: control_direct_cup_receiver_shortcut
required_controls.reason: A medium enters RV without valid screen admission and genuine passage.

required_controls.name: control_separate_washer_staging
required_controls.reason: A washer is externally supported outside FC and SC for at least 12 consecutive physics intervals.

required_controls.name: control_individual_media_robot_contact
required_controls.reason: A GR–M pair remains in contact for at least 12 consecutive physics intervals, latching invalid provenance.

required_controls.name: control_single_media_over_rim_spill
required_controls.reason: One medium exits over the screen rim; spill is immutable.

required_controls.name: control_partial_washer_escape
required_controls.reason: Any washer segment or fragment exits over the rim or crosses below the floor without genuine passage.

required_controls.name: control_fracture_fragment_loss
required_controls.reason: A fractured washer fragment is lost, invoking hard failure rather than the retained-damage cap.

required_controls.name: control_receiver_contamination
required_controls.reason: A collider in C intersects RV eroded inward by delta.

required_controls.name: control_clearance_dwell_revocation
required_controls.reason: After D=1, GR approaches within 0.060 m while F=1,r>=0.98 and other non-dwell prerequisites remain valid.

required_controls.name: control_support_dwell_revocation
required_controls.reason: After D=1, one support contact is lost while F=1,r>=0.98 and other non-dwell prerequisites remain valid.

required_controls.name: control_forbidden_state_mutation
required_controls.reason: Any post-reset task-object state write, teleport, fake weld, collider disablement, freeze, or hidden force is a permanent hard failure.

required_controls.name: control_screen_supported_contact_tolerance
required_controls.reason: F=1,r=0,D=0; all retained media and washer segments rest on the screen floor/ribs with penetration no deeper than delta and no passage or fault.

required_controls.name: control_screen_floor_breach_failure
required_controls.reason: A retained medium or washer segment crosses the floor bottom, non-aperture floor, or rib deeper than delta without genuine passage, latching spill or washer loss.

required_controls.name: control_incidental_direct_contact_exempt
required_controls.reason: F=1,r=0,D=0; one GR–M contact segment lasts 11 completed 240 Hz intervals then ends, so direct-contact provenance does not latch.

required_controls.name: control_direct_contact_threshold_fault
required_controls.reason: One GR–M or GR–WS contact pair remains true for 12 consecutive completed intervals, latching invalid provenance on the twelfth sample.

required_controls.name: control_receiver_boundary_touch_not_contamination
required_controls.reason: F=1,r>=0.98,D=0; a frozen contaminant collider only touches the RC boundary or overlaps it by at most delta and never intersects RV eroded inward by delta.

required_controls.name: control_receiver_foreign_interior_contamination
required_controls.reason: A collider from C intersects RV eroded inward by delta, latching receiver contamination; RC itself and M are excluded from C.
